The source is from the package's own declared upstream, and there's no evidence of exfiltration, remote code execution, or other malicious activities.

While the "latest" tag is unusual for a released package (version 8 suggests a fixed release), there is no evidence of injected malicious code or supply-chain compromise.

The `source` array entry fetches a tarball from `https://github.com/CallMeAlphabet/timeit/archive/refs/tags/latest.tar.gz`, which is consistent with typical AUR packaging practices, even though it uses an unpinned, mutable tag ("latest"). While this reduces reproducibility and introduces a supply-chain risk if the tag is moved, it does not constitute active malicious behavior during source fetch or PKGBUILD sourcing.

The commands `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will only source the PKGBUILD's top-level scope and execute `pkgver()` if present (which it is not here), then download and extract the source. No code in `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` will run due to the flags used. The top-level scope contains no command substitutions, `eval` calls, or immediate execution of downloaded code. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is acceptable for this audit phase, as skipping checksum verification does not imply remote code execution during fetch/extraction under `--nobuild --noprepare`.

Thus, simply sourcing the PKGBUILD and downloading the source poses no risk of executing malicious payloads or exfiltrating data.
</details>
